utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, you are still continuing examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before we continue commenting on the documents that we would like to tender, could you please tell me what the situation was in the conditions of high inflation and the problems with the changes in the currency rate. What was the possibility for persons who were working under work obligation? How could they be paid? Was it possible to pay them in goods? Was any such option likely?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must tell you that for a while we did manage to actually pay the salaries in cash. Then the soaring inflation took over, so it was difficult to secure this money, so then we resorted to paying for the people working on labour obligation and also salaries for people who worked in different companies and institutions. We paid them in goods. For example, in flour, cans, canned goods, oil, sugar, and so on. And in that way we compensated them up to a certain value for their work instead of paying them salary in cash. I must say that this lasted for quite a while. This continued even after the Dayton Peace Agreement, and even old-age pensioners up until two years ago and underprivileged persons received vouchers through which they could pay for their electricity or obtain certain goods, consumer goods which they needed in order to feed themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me a moment. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, with respect to persons who were doing work obligation in what would have been their regular place of employment before the armed conflict, such as yourself, for example, was your rate of pay the same as it was before April 17th? 1992, I should say, to be exact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It was much lower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Were you paid in cash, or were you paid in goods, the way you've described here, at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the first few months, perhaps until the autumn of 1992, I was paid in cash. And then when the inflation was rampant, then all of us were paid by various goods. All of us were compensated with goods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And just one last question: Where were all these goods coming from, the flour, the cans, the oil, the sugar, the examples that you gave? Where were these goods being acquired from in order to do such payments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the municipality we had companies. We had state- or socially-owned companies. One of them was the company Hranaprodukt, which processed fruit or vegetables. They manufactured canned foods and the agricultural cooperative also had a mill, so the grain was processed there in order to get flour. So either those companies provided the goods or we went to Tekstilac, which produced textile goods, which had their price. And based on the value of those textile goods, we would give people the goods that they required. Predominantly the goods came from socially-owned companies in our municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're on this topic, could you please tell me what the connection was or the relationship was with the republican reserve goods. Were there any interventions there in goods?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The government had the obligation of taking care of the needs of old-age pensioners. Because it wasn't able to pay them their pensions in cash, it also took goods from the companies from the territory of our municipality or Banja Luka or some other municipalities. It made up these packages, determined the value of those packages, and distributed those packages according to the lists of old-age pensioners instead of their pension.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this kind of compensation during wartime, even though you are not an economist but you can still give us your comments, was this something that was taking place in the entire territory of Republika Srpska and do you know what the situation was in the territory of the other entity, the Muslim-Croat Federation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a unified policy, and it was initiated at the government level. I have information and knowledge that the same thing was done in the Federation as well, because they had the same problem because the payment services were suspended also in the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what you personally know about the destruction of crops in the area of war operations. Why did this happen in the territory of the Samac municipality, and what were the -- what happened and what were the consequences of all of this? Who was responsible for this, and what happened? Could you please make a break just because of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the army took up a certain position - and that was the line of defence - in front and behind that line, in certain areas, some crops were already sown and they were in the way of some people. And the reason why they interfered was because they affected the visibility in the terrain where these people were. Then the brigade asked the Crisis Staff to make a decision to destroy the crops in the combat zones. The Crisis Staff adopted such a decision and instructed the Secretariat for the Economy, or the executive council, to device a plan and accompanying regulations in order for such an action to be carried out. The executive council adopted the decision and devised a plan how to destroy these crops, with the obligation that a committee should register on the ground all the destroyed crops, the quantity of the crops, and the area -- the size of the area on which such crops were destroyed, with the objective of securing compensation for the persons who owned the crops. So they wanted to cover this damage. The damage was undoubtedly caused by this. The executive council received the report from the ground about the damage, the type of crops, and the area -- the size of the area where the crops were destroyed. And then on the basis of certain parameters, using the yield of certain crops, whether it was maize or wheat, at the agricultural cooperative to determine to what extent -- how much damage was done to each individual owner and to pay out for this damage to all of those who suffered the damage. The payments for the damage were made in the course of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any differences regarding the ethnicity of the persons who had such damage done to their crops? Was there any discrimination?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no difference, no discrimination. They went in an orderly fashion from plot to plot along the line where the army had its positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When we analysed the Official Gazette, issue number 1, with some decisions from 1992, there was a decision there about some representatives or there were two articles about the National Assembly of Republika Srpska. Could you please tell me, who were the delegates to the parliament from the territory of Samac municipality in the National Assembly of Republika Srpska, if you know.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of 1992 no one was a delegate or a people's deputy from the municipality of Samac in the National Assembly of Republika Srpska. Only in 1993 was a delegate appointed or a deputy, and he was chosen from a list of deputies and he was the next person in line for this position because the previous deputy was killed. And this deputy was Mirko Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Which deputy was he, the one who was killed or the one who was elected?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He was elected Mirko Jankovic [As interpreted] as the delegate in 1993. He wasn't the one who was killed. The one who was killed was a deputy from Derventa. I'm not sure what his name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The name of Mr. Blagoje Simic and Mr. Dragic also appear there, so this is leading to some confusion. So could you please explain in what capacity, if they did go -- if any representatives did go there in 1992 or 1993, in what capacity did they go, because on the one hand we have deputies to the assembly, and then on the other hand we have two representatives, so could you please clarify this if you know.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The practice of the National Assembly then and today also is as follows: Each session of the National Assembly of Republika Srpska calls for representatives from each of the municipalities, and they are guests or observers. They meet the principal about the public nature of the work of the National Assembly, and these people could only be there as observers of the work of the National Assembly, but they didn't have any right to participate in any voting or any decision-making. This practice is still valid today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And if you know, did Dr. Blagoje Simic attend any of those assembly sessions during 1992 and 1993 in the capacity of observer or representative? Tell us if you remember. And if you don't remember, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say. I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, please tell us this: The executive council and the officials on the council, regarding them you said that your workplace was in the municipal building, meaning in the downtown; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, where was that building located and can you please tell us where was it in relation to the enemy line, to the front line. And also, please tell us in which part of the buildings were your offices. When I say "your," I mean you and other members of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a two-storey building, and it is located immediately in front of the Sava River. On the other side of the river is the Republic of Croatia. Members of our army were positioned in front of the building facing the Sava River. We members of the executive council and also employees of the administrative organs were all working on the lower floor because on one occasion I had an unpleasant experience. When I was upstairs, the shell had landed on the municipal building. It had come from Slavonski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where was that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in early 1993, and this shell landed in the toilet area and there was just one corridor dividing my office from that area. And since that time, nobody occupied offices upstairs. Therefore, all of us were downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. Mr. Lukic, if my memory serves me correctly with respect to the map of the city, the municipal building was right next door to the TO, the Territorial Defence building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a street dividing the two. On one side is the TO building, and then on the other side is the municipal assembly building. So coming from the direction of the Sava River, you would first come across the municipal assembly building. Then you would cross the street, and then you would come across the TO building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So you were familiar coming in and out of the municipal building with goings and comings into the TO building and also the SUP building. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't monitor who came in and out, but I saw that there were policemen there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have maybe a map, D27/3 in order to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Williams, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, the witness has put it in my head correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, please tell me this: In the course of 1992, were there any combat operations directed against the municipal building? Was there any firing from the machine-gun coming from the enemy side directed at the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They mostly fired from the PAM, and I have some bullet casings left. I think it's calibre 12. And they also used infantry weapons, because just some 300 to 350 metres away were the enemy positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what the PAM stands for?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an anti-aircraft weapon, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, the employees in the municipal building and members of the executive building, in view of the fact that there were positions held in front of the Sava River, can you tell me whether the employees and members of the executive council had any duty to participate in the defence and in those military operations.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We members of the executive council had no such duty, but other employees did, because the work obligation in that area covered that part of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, within the municipality, were there any fortifications or elements thereof? Was the municipal building in any way protected?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once the firing at the municipal building became quite intense, they started putting sandbags on windows, on the side facing the Sava. But even on the other side as well, because shells landed in the street and then fragments or shrapnel would be disseminated everywhere. So they started putting sandbags on all openings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps what was the number of persons who were killed in Samac municipality from the beginning till the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of those who were killed in our municipality is 750. Out of those 750, 353 are people from our municipality, our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether there were any civilians that were killed among those that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's a separate figure, that of the civilian victims, and there were about 100 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How many people in Samac municipality were wounded during the war, if you know, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the first till the tenth category, the total figure is about 1100 members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about civilians?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of civilians was around 100, the same as the number of civilians that got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of civilians that were killed and wounded in Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number, but civilians of all ethnicities got killed: Serbs, Muslims, and Croats alike. However, the majority of civilians that were killed were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what caused death and wounding of civilians?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday that shelling was quite intense. One had to go, let's say, from the municipal building home, and no one knew when shells would be falling. I remember one situation where a neighbour of mine, a policeman, got killed on his way from the police station to his apartment. He was near the department store when a shell landed and got killed. His name was Savo Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What measures were taken in order to rebuild the residential facilities in 1992 and in 1993 in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, a lot of housing facilities were damaged, especially in the town itself, but also in villages that were closer to the town, such as Orasje, Domaljevac, or those that were closer to Croatia, to Slavonski Samac. The Crisis Staff passed a decision to establish a construction company, and the Secretariat for Economy established and registered the company, whose main task was to repair as much as was possible as many buildings as possible with the material that we had at our disposal. They had to do that without in fact decreasing the residential area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now we will turn to a different topic that has to do with activities of the executive council. I will ask you to comment on some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we shall discuss now a document with our internal number D002.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday you already gave us several comments regarding the work obligation. Now I would like to know the following: Which organ of the municipal structure addressed the Secretariat of People's Defence and what was the mechanism involved there? Could you please give us a few comments regarding this request.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff passed a decision on the functioning of the economy in wartime and approved the operation of a certain number of socially-owned companies. The Secretariat for Economy within the executive council was tasked with reviving these socially-owned companies. Naturally this was to be done in cooperation with the coordinators in the companies that had been appointed by the Crisis Staff. In order for a company to start working and in order for it to operate, they needed workers within their work obligation. Therefore, a coordinator would make a list of employees that were necessary and ask the Secretariat for Defence and the Secretariat for Economy in order for them to provide the number of employees that was needed in order to start production in a certain company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this now: Based on this document, what were the business hours of people performing their work obligation? Here I have in mind the company called Tekstilac and the veterinary station in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A decision was passed on business hours --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. Please tell us regarding this document that you have in front of you right now.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the decision on business hours, it was stated that the business hours from 8.00 till 18.00 hours, the coordinator in cooperation with the Secretariat for Economy was supposed to pass a decision on business hours; however, his decision could not specify longer business hours that had been previously determined by the previous decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at this document in front of you. Tell me what were the business hours of the veterinary station.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, the coordinator had proposed and the Secretary for Economy had agreed to specify that the business hours in this organisation would be not longer than eight hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that was the norm, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a majority of socially-owned companies, people worked for eight hours a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another question regarding this document. It stems from paragraph 2 of this document. It mentions here permits for movement. Can you tell me, please, who was in charge of it. Was it the police or some other authority? If you know, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who had a work obligation had to have a permit to move around. This permit was issued to me, to the president of the executive council, to employees, and to everybody else by the Public Security Station. If it applied to members of the army, then the relevant command would issue permits to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if there is no objection, I would like to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Your Honours, it's D77/1 and D77/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, now we have a document D004/1, 2, and 3. In fact, there are three documents, so I would like to have the guidelines from the Trial Chamber. They are speaking about the same issue, about the work obligation. And all three documents were issued on the 20th of June, 1992. So could we have maybe one exhibit possible, one exhibit number, with dividing of A, B, or C, or 1, 2, or 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'll leave that to the registry assistant, I think. And if there are no objections to the Prosecution, then they may not stand up. They should only stand up if they're objecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I would just say there is no objection to the material Mr. Pantelic has advised us which he is putting to the witness at all. Two of them we don't have English translations [Realtime transcript read in error "we don't have translations"], but I sure Mr. Pantelic can deal with that at the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. We can discuss that time and taking care about that. So Ms. Registrar, what would be your suggestion since we have three basically same documents? Should we have one exhibit number and then /1, 2, 3 or...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It should then be D78/1, D78A/1, D78B/1, and D78C/1 with the ter for the respective B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to discuss very shortly this exhibit with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just correct something on the transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The transcript says that I said we don't have translations. I said we don't have translations of two documents. Mr. Pantelic has provided us with translations of the balance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just a few brief comments. You have already explained to us how this system of the work obligation functioned, so we're not going to deal with this any more. However, I should be interested in hearing you on the following: If you know, the persons who are stated under numbers 1 to 4, what ethnicity are they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know all of them, and they're all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So what kind of system was this that we see here in the text, "8+8+8," and which concerned Serbs in this decision specifically?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons here were members of the military. They participated in the army, but they also owned land, owned their farms. In order to organise production, they were prepared to spend eight hours with the military to have an eight-hour work obligation on the farm and to have the remaining eight hours for rest and recuperation. So we sent this request to the Secretariat for People's Defence, and in cooperation with their brigade, that is, their unit, they complied with this request.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The other two documents, one concerns the Zivinokop company, and the other the Master company. I think your comment would be the same; however, if you have anything in particular to add in respect of these two documents, please do.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the situation is more or less the same. Here we have a large farm in Donji Zabar, which is the subject of this particular request. The other document concerns the work obligation in the state of owned company called Master, in which the coordinator is asking the Secretariat for Economy to contact the Secretariat for People's Defence and to give work obligation assignments to these four individuals. As far as I know them, I think that they are mechanics, people who are involved in car maintenance. And Master was a transport company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In case of this last decision, we see that there is no mention of other options such as 8+8+8. I assumed that the working hours are the usual ones.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, the usual business hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the penultimate paragraph we see that for the needs of the military a certain amount of work is to be performed. Who had the priority in wartime in respect of certain particular assignments, the civilian part or the military part, if a work was to be done?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the military and the police who always had the priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Ms. Registrar, now we should discuss document D005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was advised from my colleagues -- you mean exhibit number for this document, Mr. Re, or for the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the previous one. I was just waiting for some exhibit numbers so we can record them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have D78/1 A, B, C.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the record can we just find out which document is which, A, B, and C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the registry assistant could repeat them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I followed the sequence as they were given. There is an annotation of 88/, 89/, 90/ on top of each English translation. I can give the titles. "Request for work assignment," that will be D78A/1 and ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It has an "88" figure on the right-hand corner on the English translation. The next -- well, since they have all the same title and the same date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's easier to distinguish them -- because each document has got a different -- if you read handwritten on the right-hand corner on the top, one has 89, one has 88, one has 90. If the Prosecution are observing that. Yes. So the registry assistant, yes, followed that sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, what can you tell us in respect of this particular document? First of all, have you already seen this document? What is this document? Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen such documents. We had a number of similar requests. A moment ago I told you about this construction company. And this village here was located in the vicinity of the separation line. And the same as the town was exposed to intense shelling from the positions of the Croatian army. The people here, the owners of the houses there, are asking for help with the reconstruction and the repair work to be performed on their houses in order to prevent further damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was this request made?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The document is signed by the commissioner. What was the role of the commissioner in local communes in particular?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the -- to help you with the title, this used to be the president of the local commune before the war, who in wartime became the commissioner. It is a civilian person who is supposed to take care of the everyday life of the given local commune in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One additional question for the record -- no, it's already been translated, I see. Just help us with the handwritten text at the bottom of the page, page 2. Do you know by any chance who signed this text and what is this note all about?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can read, the text is as follows: "A complete request -- or to complete the request." And here we see the employees of the Secretariat for Economy, according to whom the request has been complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D79/1 and D79/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So now I have again a document. I will just make a short description. It's D009, and then there are four documents. Basically these are the pay lists. The first document that I will discuss -- also we could have the same approach, because it relates to the same -- to the same company. The first document is the payroll for month of May 1992 with nine -- in total with the nine workers, nine names. The second document is a payroll for month of June 1992, with eight names in total. We are speaking about the company 11th of April. That's the name of the company, on the top left-hand corner. The third document is also for the same company. It's a payroll for July, in total with six persons. And finally, there is one handwritten document, also for company 11th of April, for the month of April 1992, in total with 13 persons. So that we can follow these documents. Is it okay with the Prosecution? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, just one clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: You just mentioned the last one there, the handwritten document also for the company called the 11th of April. And then you said it's for the month of April 1992. But just looking at the translation, the dates seem to be stamped differently. For example, on page 1 of the English translation, we've got, "List of employees who worked in July," for example. And on the next page, "List of employee who is worked in June." I simply raise that because you said it was for April, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Because in one -- yes. I do apologise, Your Honour. Yes, you are right. There are also handwritten documents for June and -- let me check. It's June and July. Yes. But the first document is for the month of April but it's not translated here. It's -- you can see on the translation where 13 persons are listed and the first name is Kosta Mihaljcic and then in brackets you have (expansion unknown) which is Roman number IV on original, on the top right-hand corner, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, so you have this payroll for the month of May 1992 in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The company we're concerned with is the 11th of April.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a utility company which was state owned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was it involved in?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it was a utility company which was in charge of maintaining the town, in charge of sanitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, if you know whether on this list we find the people who prior to April 1992 had worked in this company.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know some of them, and I think yes, they had worked in this company prior to the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell us about the procedure regarding salaries. I see the relevant municipal stamp at the bottom of the page. Was the same principle as the one that you explained yesterday applied in this case as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same principle applied for all the work obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at -- please look at this handwritten document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Usher. It's the handwritten document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please placed on the ELMO. I think it's the third or fourth document. This column all the way to the right with all of these dashes or the 4/3 numbers, do you know what that could indicate? If you don't know what it means, the last column on the right, say so.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the code number of the chequing account card of their bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But it's confusing because these "8s" or these numbers are the same for several persons, and that would mean that all of those people have one account or perhaps they were paid through the cashier. So just tell us if you know. But if you don't know, you don't need to dwell on this in any detail.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't paid by the cashier because it does have the sign that it was checked by the payment system service. It could only be some kind of code, and this is maybe a sign that the company provided chequing books for its workers. I don't understand what this "3" stands for in all the entries. Maybe that should be a different number. I cannot really confirm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is what the counsel told you, that if you don't know, you say you don't know. Because we want information where you are certain, not where you are guessing. So if you don't know the details, what they mean, then you say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Ms. Registrar, could we have a number for these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The payroll from May 1992 will be D80A/1 and ter for the respective B/C/S version. The payroll for June 1992 will be D80B/1 and ter. The payroll of July 1992 will be D80C/1 and ter. And the two-pages-long document, beginning with 13 names for payroll, will be D80D/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Registrar. Could we have now the next document, which is internal number D0010. And it consists of -- it's also payrolls. It consists of three documents for the month of May 1992, June 1992, and July 1992. It's a Samac fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Basically, Mr. Lukic, we have already discussed these documents quite considerably, so we will not really dwell on them for too long. But could you please give me your following -- your comment on the following. Did the fire-fighters or the fire brigade in Samac have some kind of special status, in view of their duties?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nothing changed regarding the fire-fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just like in other towns and systems, I assume, this is a very special, very serious job, particularly in time of war.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And they had a lot of problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you now please look at these three payroll sheets and tell me briefly -- we won't go into any details about that -- what was the ethnic composition of the fire-fighting unit in Samac in the period of May, June, and July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say here that the names are of people of all three ethnicities. The majority of those people are still fire-fighters in the fire brigade in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did they come back to Samac after the war or did they spend the entire time in Samac while the war was going on in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the fire brigade the entire time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we -- thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have an exhibit number, please, Ms. Registrar, for these three payroll lists for the month of May, June, and July 1992, these.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be D81A/1 and ter, D81B/1 and ter, and D81C/1 and ter respectively. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now our document with internal number D0011, consisting of three payroll lists for the month of June, with a list of 22 persons, two pages for June. And then also -- and this is -- these are the representatives or commissioners in local communes on the territory of municipality of Bosanski Samac. Then the next document is on the top left-hand corner related to local commune Upper Slatina, with five persons. And the last one is a document, number 4701/92, dated 3rd of June, 1992, issued by executive board also with 23 subjects or persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, this document speaks for itself. The number of persons on it is 22 for the month of July. You already said something about the role of the commissioner.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The month of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, up until what time period were these commissioners active? This is June. Were they active after that month or was this issue resolved in a different way?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commissioners were representatives of the local communes, and they were active until the first elections were held in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Relating to the period before April 1992, did the presidents of the local communes or those officials receive salaries from the budget for their work? Could you please tell us how many local communes comprise a municipality and what are the budgetary obligations between the municipality and the local communes.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 17th of April, 1992 the presidents of the local communes were on the local commune budget, because until that time, they had their own source of financing. Each local commune levied the local self-tax or contribution. Whether this was for the land register matters or something -- a tax regarding property. But in any case, they determined such taxes on the local level and then based on those funds, financial funds were paid out to the presidents of those local communes. Because this was no longer possible, their expenses or salaries were covered by the municipal budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have another question while looking at this list. In June 1992, except for the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac, was there another municipality with the same name, "Municipality of Bosanski Samac"?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croats formed their own municipality from a part of the Bosanski Samac municipality. It was called Domaljevac Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't see the Prud local commune on this list. Who controlled Prud in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was part of the municipality of Odzak, because they were across the River Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which ethnic group was in control of that territory?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croats and Muslims. And at that time the population there was 99 per cent Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the pre-war territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, after April 17th, 1992, in that period, was divided into three parts.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the parts that you mentioned, Domaljevac and Prud, you said that those parts were inhabited by which ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were inhabited by Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where did they live before April 1992? And I'm thinking of those two parts of the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the local communes of the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did Croat citizens live in those local communes before April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And of course after April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have a number for these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be D82A/1, D82B/1 and D82C/1 and ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I inquire which document has which number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Following the dates that were given by Mr. Pantelic, June 1992 and the way that the documents were introduced, and the first list introduced was the list of 22 names. The second list introduced by Mr. Pantelic was the list of June 1992 with five names, and the third list, with 23 names. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Registrar. I believe we are -- we have another document which is RH34. I do apologise. There are some problems. We shall follow the -- Ms. Registrar. I do apologise. There's a problem with the line of documents. No, it's okay. But in future we shall resolve that. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me briefly, since the executive council adopted this decision, what was the purpose of this decision?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As winter was coming, the majority of the population was engaged in the army. And on the other hand, there were sections of the population that were unable to secure their own firewood. The executive council charged the Secretariat for Economy to prepare a decision in order to be prepared for the coming winter. So those sections of the population unable to secure their own firewood and who did not have their own woods or timber were to receive firewood through this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, did the families have to pay for this firewood?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government passed a decree regarding the firewood in which it was stated that the timber farms could provide certain quantities and then families had to pay for it. In view of the situation that we had in our municipality, the economic affairs, the financial affairs and so on, we decided to distribute firewood to certain categories of the population without any compensation. Therefore, those who received firewood did not in fact have to pay for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at Article 6 of this decision. I assume that it sets forth the categories of the population that were eligible to receive firewood; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are criteria that defined who was eligible to receive firewood, and it listed these categories in the order of priority they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Does this decision in a way give any priority to any ethnic group with respect to receiving firewood?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that the main idea was to first provide firewood to families of fallen soldiers and war veterans and handicapped veterans, and that following that everybody else received the same quantities regardless of their ethnic background. In order to compile these categories, the lists of the centre for social work were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This manner of distributing firewood to residents of Samac, did it only apply in 1992 or perhaps in the following years as well? Can you tell us until when was this manner of distributing firewood applied?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war years. That means 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995. In winters of those years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in these following years, after 1992, was it applied differently to different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Registrar, could we have a number, please, for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The decision of 17th September, 1992 will be Exhibit D83/1 and D83/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe -- the next document is RH5. Is it the first, Ms. Registrar, number that you have in your box? RH5. Is it okay? Did we catch the right line? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This copy in barely legible, unfortunately, but please tell me what was the basis for the executive council to pass this decision. But prior to that, please tell me who signed this decision, if you know.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of this decision?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we are an agricultural area, we conducted preparations and made plans for spring and autumn crop sowing, and this is one kind of a plan for spring sowing in 1993. The objective was to procure fuel for farmers at good prices, and the municipality in fact compensated for the difference between the price at which they were provided fuel and the market price.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: We are now talking about RH5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: RH5, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes. And the -- Mr. Lukic said that the signature is his, but it's signed by Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you please explain to His Honour Lindholm this issue.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was vice-president of the executive council, which means that in the absence of the president during the session of the executive council, I substituted for him. And right here above you can see an indication that stands for "upon authority." Milan Simic was the president of the executive council, and upon authority I was the one who signed this, based or pursuant to the law on general administrative procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This abbreviation, "PO," what you just told us, was this in fact the abbreviation, PO?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you know, please tell us: When it comes to the way the state organs function, in view of the large number of documents they have to deal and so on, is it usual that a procedure was established for somebody to sign these documents in the absence of the relevant persons?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the secretariats, the secretary was able to authorise somebody to sign documents on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And just one more question before the break: At that time, in 1993, the price of 1 litre of oil, was it a real market price of 1 Deutschmark for 1 litre?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I explained to you that this was not that kind of a price. This was a price that was determined without VAT. The municipality covered for the difference for the VAT. That means that the retail price was lower than 1 convertible mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this manner of procuring fuel, procuring oil, did it apply to farmers of all ethnicities or were there any priorities there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied to all farmers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Regardless of their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no discrimination whatsoever. That means regardless of their ethnicity, everybody was able to procure oil at the price of 1 mark for a litre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D84/1 and D84/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I believe it's time for our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will continue our proceedings at 16.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to discuss document -- the internal number is RH7, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The copy is very poor, and I apologise for that. But can you discern to whom was this memo sent?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see here, the Secretariat for Economy of our municipality informs the Ministry for Agricultural, waterworks, and forestry, that certain areas had been prepared for autumn sowing of crops, various crops, and in order to harvest these crops, 600 tonnes of fuel would be needed, which means that the Ministry for Agricultural had to give a consent to import or otherwise provide this amount of fuel for our municipality for the autumn harvesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before we go on, could I ask for the clarity of the record so that we know exactly what has been tendered, that perhaps my learned friend can read onto the record what document he's referring to or maybe the assistant registrar so that it matches up with the exhibit number. Because at the moment it says "RH7," which of course won't appear in any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So what you want is the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The party introducing it will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do apologise. So the document is actually -- on the top left-hand corner, number -- internal number is 3/08, 1992. And it's dated the 12th of October, 1992. The title is some kind of letter with regard to the fuel for autumn harvest. Is that sufficient for ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask you this, Mr. Lukic: Was it typical for something like this to go on between the Ministry of Agriculture and the relevant municipal organ, in terms of procuring fuel? I would like to know whether this was successful, successfully accomplished in reality, or was it simply limited to correspondence on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat for Economy had to send to the Ministry of Agricultural, Waterworks, and Forestry, a report on plans for sowing and harvesting. In these reports, in addition to information on areas planted, they also had to propose certain measures that applied to those areas, whether it had to do with fuel, seeds, or pesticides, and so on. They had to report on this. And sometimes the government replied to these memos and sometimes it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Here is my next question: During those war years, was the agricultural activity proceeding regularly in terms of spring and autumn activity in the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout all of those years. Some years more areas were planted; some years fewer areas were planted, depending on the war operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was the principle of work obligation also applied to these activities in view of extensive agricultural areas and the labour that was needed there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We secured in this manner a large quantity of wheat, which was later on ground into flour. As for the corn, it was used for cattle feed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were some of these works carried out through the work obligation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this work obligation apply to all residents, regardless of their ethnicity, or were there some different approaches made there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied to all residents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you please finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied to all citizens of our municipality regardless of their ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could I have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D85/1 and D85/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next document is RH8, a document with internal number 712/92, dated 11th of July, 1992. This is a authorisation signed by the Secretary for Economy, Municipal Secretary for Economy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, maybe we should say authorisation for the work of the mill.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the work of the mill. Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a very brief comment on this decision. What were the reasons for its adoption and so on?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This consent, this approval relates to the decision on the work of the agriculture in wartime. This approval was not given initially. It was given only subsequently. However, an obligation was placed on the owner to make this mill operational, so that this part of the territory of the municipality could function appropriately, could provide adequate services of milling, of grinding for cattle food.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the introductory part of this approval. I'm interested in this portion of the text where it says, "The involvement or the engagement of the citizens in wartime," in relation to this type of work.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was necessary for someone to transport the corn to the mill. It is a bulk cargo, and the able-bodied men, most of them were already otherwise engaged, so other measures had to be taken. Other arrangements had to be found so that this type of services can be appropriately given.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D86/1 and D86/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is RH11, internal number of the document is on the top left-hand corner, 2973/92, dated 3rd of October, 1992. It's a decision on the organised collection of foreign currency for agricultural activities, issued -- this document was issued by the executive board -- municipal executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly, Mr. Lukic, if you can tell us what the purpose of this decision was.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision is closely related to the decisions we commented a moment ago, concerning the procurement of fuel at the pretext price. These agricultural collectives were in charge of sowing and harvesting work, and they were under the obligation of obtaining a specified amount of fuel at the price of 1 convertible mark with the proviso that the agricultural workers had to pay that amount of money depending on the area that they were supposed to cultivate, depending on the extent of the land involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This procedure, did it function in practice? I am referring to the activities of the agricultural collectives. And what was further undertaken to complete this job?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This type of work, concerning agricultural work, functioned adequately throughout that period of time, which means that the agricultural collectives organised this type of production in addition to all other activities related to the agricultural work. And on the basis of the information provided by those collectives, the relevant data as to the necessary quantity of the fuel were obtained, including also the resources that were necessary to buy this amount of fuel for the agricultural work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D87/1 and D87/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is internal number RH12. This is a document issued by executive -- municipal executive board, internal number 2961/92, dated 3rd of October, 1992. It's an information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, is it also related to the procedure you just explained to us? Tell us, please, if you recognise this type of document. Did you ever come into contact with this type of document in the course of your work?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D88/1 and D88/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now it's RH14. It's a decision rendered by the executive -- municipal executive board. The internal number is 337/92, dated 16th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have already told us about the way the salaries were paid. In Article 1, we see that it concerns the people who had the right to be issued specified salaries in various work organisations. Is that the essence of Article 1?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the Article 5, please, of this decision. What does this article regulate? What kind of procedural arrangements, as far as salaries are concerned are specified here?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, there are two categories of the beneficiaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you briefly comment on this, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that a number of socially-owned companies organised production and were making profit with ready-made products, they were able to pay their employees according to the work obligation that they had in those companies. However, there was a number of other companies, such as the utility company, the fire brigade, and a few others, that were not able to charge for their services. Therefore, they were on the budget list of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 9 of this decision, please, governed, I assume, the relevant time frame work. It specifies the period of time that this principle was applied.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean, the decision was adopted on the 16th of June. What was the reason for the adoption of this decision, if you can tell us that, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The salaries were not paid right away. Therefore, they had to be paid retroactively. That is the reason for this retroactive mode of payment as specified in this decision. It is all about the rights of the beneficiaries of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D89/1 and D89/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us move to another subject. We will go back to these matters once again, but let me now focus on something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... issued by executive board or committee, internal number 2750/93, 13th of September, 1993, conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and tell us the basis for this decision.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was reached upon the following bases: It was the obligation of the utility and environment company, had to do with the following -- I mean, this person here forcefully moved into someone else's property. Prior to that he did not have appropriate decision, that is, an approval for the temporary use of premises, and no mention was also made on the adequate commission having worked on this. And I was informed that this individual had illegally moved into abandoned property, and I issued an order for the utility and environment company to evict this illegal tenant from this property.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What ethnicity is this person?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ranko Mitrovic, a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were there any other similar cases involving persons who had illegally - and I'm talking to the period of time 1992 and 1993 - who had illegally moved into somebody else's property outside the criteria specified for the use of abandoned property?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember such cases. They involved also members of the military, other people who wanted to swap their apartments, who moved from smaller apartments to larger apartments. All kinds of persons were involved in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, if there were any cases of complaints addressed to municipal authorities by non-Serbs and were any protective measures undertaken with the view of protecting their rights.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Usually they addressed themselves to the utility and -- housing, utility, and environmental company, and then that secretariat would inform the police station thereon so that the police could take appropriate steps in order to evict such individuals, that is, to provide adequate assistance in the case -- in cases when the individuals in question were resisting -- did not want to leave on their own this property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. I think for the sake of clarity -- it might be a question of translation. The exhibit or the document in front of us talks about this conclusion being addressed to the municipal Secretariat for Housing, Public Utilities, Special Planning, and Urban Development. But what we're getting in the translation on two occasions, at page 37, line 25 and then also on page 38, line 17 and 18, is something called the utility and housing and environmental company being asked to evict people. Now, that seems a little bit strange. Are we talking about the same thing and it's just a question in the translation that we're talking about a company, as opposed to this municipal secretariat, which was part of the government in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do believe, Your Honour, it's a question of maybe translation. But maybe Mr. Lukic can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Municipal Secretariat for Housing and Communal Affairs and Spatial Planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's clarified that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one other question with respect to the same document: This Mr. Mitrovic, who is going to be evicted, the property that he was in, from reading this it doesn't appear to be a private residence, because it was going to be used to allow the elementary school to resume class instruction. Could you just say very briefly in just a few words what was this building he was in that he was going to be evicted from. It's called the Dva Lovca building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a private house. Dva Lovca is a cafe on the ground floor. The cafe is on the ground floor and the first floor is a housing unit and we're talking about a private house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I suppose my question really related to this eviction. It seems to have been to allow the elementary school to resume its classes without interruption. That's why I was questioning what was the nature of this property. But you say it's a private -- a private house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a private house. And since the school was relocated, the school operated in this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, the name of this cafe is "Two Hunters," just for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number please for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D90/1 and D90/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now it's the document RH17. It's a pay list for the month of May for the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac. May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this document, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the employees in the municipal bodies, in the municipality for the month of May.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So in the period of the month of May, this was actually the municipal government, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were the members of the executive council and the people who were employed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then depending on the growth of the secretariat, this number of employees grew.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, depending on the requirements and the larger number of employees in the executive council, this number grew.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe this is not important, but I'm interested. Why is the number in the second column on the right crossed out and then there is another number that is not crossed out that is less than the previous amount? I'm just asking you out of curiosity. Maybe it's not that important.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This first number that is crossed out is -- actually, there's a mistake here. It says, "The president of the executive council." But actually, there was no president. But had there been a president, he would have received this amount of 51.000. And that's why there is a smaller number here, because it wasn't the post -- he wasn't carrying out the post of the president of the executive council, so the cashier made a mistake, thinking that there was such a function at the time, president of the executive council, but there wasn't in fact, so this is why that number was crossed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In relation to the range of salaries in accordance with the regulations, did the salaries actually keep to this range?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were within the range, but they were lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar, could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D91/1 and D91/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is our internal number is RH19. And this is a decision issued by the executive board or committee. Without internal number, only /92, dated 10th of September, 1992, consisting of three pages. Decision on the organised execution of autumn agriculture work and the tariffs of services in the Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't think we have a translation for this one. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have -- I have one copy for you. Yes, thank you. It was not a bad intention for our friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, could you please tell me the following: I see here in the preamble some markings or some indications for these regulations. Could you please tell us what was the basis for these regulations. What does this regulation contain, this regulation of the government from the 31st of July, 1992. Could you please tell us this very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government, as you said, on the 31st of July, 1991 made this decision on the engaging of citizens to collect the harvest and instructed the municipalities to prepare municipal decisions in line with this decision. The secretariat prepared this decision and set here the price list for the works carried out, i.e., for compensation to be paid to persons who participated in this work, in the implementation of the spring and autumn planting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is clear to me. It's wartime. Please tell me --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These rates are symbolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, Mr. Lukic, in Article 2 of this decision, item 2, land from abandoned territories is mentioned. Can you please explain to me what these abandoned territories are and what was the purpose of carrying out these autumn agricultural works there, if you know.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agricultural ministry made a decision about the manner in which abandoned land would be used in terms of agricultural work in the municipalities. That means that people who left the territory, leaving their property behind, their land, so that this land would not be overgrown with weeds or go fallow, this land was given for temporary use for cultivation and for spring and autumn planting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now I'm interested in Article 3. The labour required to carry out these activities is talked about here. Before the war, in the municipality of Samac were there any broader organised activities in any extraordinary circumstances or during spring or summer planting? And did this happen in the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only during floods. That's when there were some activities during a state of emergency. This is when these headquarters were activated and when they applied this manner of organisation. Everything else was done individually, but the government decree regulates - and that's this decree here - and it states in the preamble that in this way as much land as possible had to be processed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who was included in this labour force when we look at Article 3?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who were fit or able to take part in the work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, just look at Article 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Agricultural machinery was requisitioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the labour force.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unemployed women, men, children and men, the labour force from the work detachments and the labour detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. So this category, did that apply to all of the population regardless of their ethnicity or were there any differences in the way these works were organised?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This applied to the entire population, and everybody was included in this activity. This related to all of the population regardless of their ethnicity. And when they talk about children, what is meant are children over 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I assume that the reason for this was that because so many people were engaged in military duties, so there was no other way to organise these activities.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to explain this further, there wasn't enough of the population that was fit to work, so depending on the activities that had to be carried out, this group of the population was engaged to actually carry out these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 4 provides for some type of compensation. Was this part applied, and what can you tell us about that? Because this work should have been evaluated in some way.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the list of rates, according to which those who participated in these autumn works were compensated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was subsequently done? Since there were some socially-owned enterprises and socially-owned land as well, what was subsequently done with those products after the harvest was carried out? How were they distributed, these goods? How was this arranged?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
