utterances.text: When we're talking about socially-owned enterprises, the wheat and the maize was taken to the silo in the agricultural cooperative. When we were talking about individuals, this was either given to the agricultural cooperative or kept by the owner in his own storage facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar, could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D92/1 and D92/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now document RH20. This is a decision -- basically the same issues. It was issued by executive board on 23rd of June, 1992, document consisting of three pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, basically this is the same kind of procedure except that this decision was reached in June 1992. I'm interested in Article 2 here and in this term "mobilised combine harvesters." How did this procedure function and who organised this requisition or mobilisation of combine harvesters? Who organised it and what was the purpose of that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Crisis Staff reached its decision to carry out the harvest works, the executive committee or the Secretariat for the Economy devised the way in which the harvest was going to be carried out. Since wheat had to be cut from the ground, we had to engage the combine harvesters from individual owners, even though socially-owned enterprises had a number of combine harvesters, the agricultural cooperative had that, but they didn't have enough. So the local communes and the municipality were tasked with making a list of all the combine harvesters in the local communes and via the Secretariat for National Defence -- or People's Defence to activate these agricultural machines so that the wheat could be cut from the fields as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was this manner of temporary exception or sparing of people from military service in order to participate in these works something that was typically done during wartime?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Secretariat for Defence conducted mobilisation of such vehicles or machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at Article 11 on page 3. Item 1 has a part that was typed in and handwritten. Now, please, can you tell us what are Napredak and Pik, and what did this first paragraph mean in relation to the flour that had been collected.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two socially-owned enterprises had their own land, which they used to sow certain crops. And then this decision specified that these crops would be dried in their own silos and would later on be used or be distributed to the population or to the military as specified in this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, what happened with the privately-owned wheat? Did private farmers also have an obligation to turn over their grain for these purposes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar, could we have a number, please, for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D93/1 and D93/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is RH22. It's a conclusion issued by the executive board on 12th of February, 1993. "Conclusion to nominate candidates for the organs of the chamber of the economy of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, please tell me, what was the basis for this decision which was passed in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This signifies that the Chamber of Commerce had started operating and that our municipality had to provide -- or had to send certain people to the Chamber of Commerce and its organs. It says here that Stanko Djurdjevic and another person are being nominated as representatives to the assembly of the Chamber of Commerce.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, let us now take a look at item 3 of this decision and please tell me whether this is your name mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What were you nominated for then?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was vice-president of the executive council; however, the president of the executive council did not attend this particular session and therefore I signed the decision on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no, I'm interested in item 3 on page 2 of this document. And the copy is quite poor, so please take a look at this and tell me what body and -- what body is mentioned here and whether this is your name mentioned here as a candidate for this body.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber of Commerce had an honourable court which numbered five people, and I was among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please, an exhibit number for this document, Ms. Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D94/1 and D94/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document that I would like to discuss is RH23. This is a decision issued by the executive board dated -- decision to appoint a commission to draft a decision on provisional funding of general, public and joint requirements, dated 6th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, please tell me about this commission and what is this temporary funding all about. What was the purpose of this decision?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This commission was tasked with preparing a draft budget for 1993, especially emphasising the funding of general universal needs. They had to specify what was to be funded from the budget of the municipal assembly for that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did the municipal assembly already start functioning as an institution at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had already started functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D95/1 and D95/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is RH25. It's an order issued by the order on the method of changing the prices of certain products and services in Samac municipality, rendered by the executive committee or board on 28th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another decision passed in 1993. Please tell us briefly if you know, what was the reason for this? In Article 1 there is an Official Gazette of Republika Srpska mentioned, so please tell us what is this about.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government of Republika Srpska in order to protect the living standard of the population had established the restrictions on prices for basic goods and specified in Article 2 that the prices can be changed only upon the approval of the executive council, providing that there was an additional written explanation given, which means that such goods as bread, water, electric power, flour, and so on, these basic goods are what this decision applied to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did the executive council in Samac monitor prices of these vital goods, basic consumer goods, in Samac during wartime?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D96/1 and D96/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this document is RH26. It's a decision on the working hours of the executive committee and administration organs, issued on 18th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us not dwell on this too long. This is a decision that was passed after the previous one, and I can see that business hours are reduced here.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The working conditions are improving. There is even a mention of a breakfast break. So please tell me, what did all this signify, this reduction in business hours?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meant that the situation became more normal, that organs started functioning in a normal way, and that the executive council found it appropriate to introduce regular eight-hour working days, and this was accomplished in stages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D97/1 and D97/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. The next document is RH28. This is a decision issued by the executive board on the 13th of January, 1993 on introducing measures to remove emergency conditions in the following companies, Samac, Bosanka, Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The copy is very bad, Mr. Lukic, and I regret this. However, I don't have a better copy. But please tell me this: What are emergency conditions in enterprises? What does this apply to? But first, tell me this: Samac, Bosanka, Velepromet, and so on are these private companies or are they differently owned?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that these are socially-owned companies. These are municipal enterprises.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, please tell me, what were these extraordinary circumstances mentioned here? It is said here that in the past there were extraordinary circumstances, and now in January 1993 this situation no longer applied.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state of war existed in the past. The war was on, and the situation was a true emergency. And later on as the time passed, things became more normal, and then we switched from a centralised system to a decentralised one, both in enterprises and in institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since three of these enterprises started operating as one, as is mentioned here in paragraph 1, they started operating as Samcanka, I would now like to turn to Article 5 of this decision, where the competencies of the executive council are discussed. So please tell me what competencies the executive council had when it came to appointment of managers and executives in these socially-owned enterprises. Very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until that time the appointment of coordinators was conducted by the Crisis Staff. Afterwards, or rather, in 1993 already, this role was taken over by the executive council. And this was done just on the basis of rational functioning. Three companies, three enterprises that existed before the war were now joined into one in order not to have three administrations and so on. All of these enterprises were socially owned, and they provided goods for the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this new company, does it still exist under the same name today, and is it still owned by the state, by the municipality, or has the ownership of it been changed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until recently, it existed under the same name, Samcanka. However, two or three months ago the state capital of that enterprise was sold and sold to private owners.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D98/1 and D98/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is RH29. It's a conclusion on activating all production and other economic capacities in the area of the municipality, issued on the 28th of January, 1993 by the executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Mr. Lukic, what was the objective of this decision?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We in the executive council analysed the situation both on the ground and in the vicinity, and based on that we passed a conclusion which instructed Secretary for Economy to cooperate with directors of enterprises and ensure that enterprises produced the maximum amount of products, to ensure that they functioned at the maximum levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about these companies in Samac? Do you know whether managers and executives in those companies in 1992 and 1993 belonged to all three ethnic groups or was the situation different? I am now referring to publicly-owned companies.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I touched upon this issue yesterday, but I can repeat this again. The director of Uniglas was Asim Zaimbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what is his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about other companies?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mebos the director was a Croat. The director of the medical centre was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D99/1 and D99/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is RH30. This is a decision amending the decision of the organising execution of the autumn agriculture work, and the tariffs of services in Samac municipality, dated 6th of November, 1992, issued by the executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This decision also concerns the subject that you have addressed. It was adopted in November. Tell us if you will, Article 1 makes mention of a number of categories of persons. What does this refer to, please, if you can explain?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 1 amended the decision which we commented a moment ago. It concerns autumn agricultural work, namely, the work that had to be done in relation to the families of fallen soldiers and war veterans, including invalids, those who were undergoing medical treatment, for instance. In order to secure this type of work free of charge -- I am referring to the autumn agricultural work which was to be performed on the land of these families free of charge -- the municipality according to this decision would participate in providing the necessary resources, such as fuel, lubricants, and so on and so forth, for the purposes of conducting this type of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this decision concern only one ethnic community, or did it apply equally to all citizens irrespective of their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied equally to all citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D100/1 and D100/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document I would like to discuss is RH33, consisting of seven pages, and the English translation should be also, I believe, seven pages. This is a document, it's a decision on the determination of economic entities, type and volume of activity. The entities will engage at wartimes in organisation of activity of such entities. Dated May 27, 1992, issued by the executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although at the time you did not hold this office, if I'm not mistaken - this is dated May 27th - can you tell us, please, what you know about this decision. What particular service was in charge of drafting this decision and what was its purpose?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Crisis Staff that reached the decision on the work of the economy in wartime. And on the basis of their decision, it was necessary to make appropriate arrangements as to which particular economic entities were concerned, which particular departments, which particular areas, and so on and so forth; that is, who exactly was supposed to be involved in this type of work. We have a non-exhaustive list of such entities from the area of agriculture, construction, economy, craftsmanship, and so on and so forth. The decision specifies which entities are involved, that is, who exactly can be engaged in this type of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the purpose was to have -- to identify priorities in the field of agriculture and economy.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A certain number of companies or economic entities has to be involved, and it was necessary to organise this type of work as soon as possible, and it was the Secretariat for Economy that was engaged in this type of decision-making in view of the relevant area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D101/1 and D101/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document that I'd like to discuss with Mr. Lukic is R19. It's -- actually, the act issued by the government of Serbian Republic of BH. It's an extract from the Official Gazette of Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina, published in number 12, and dated 31st July 1992. "Instructions on implementing the decree on the compulsory handover of spoils of war and spoils acquired by other means to the republican commodity reserves."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, tell us please whether you were familiar with this instruction at the time in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was adopted in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My first question was whether it was binding for the municipal bodies, municipal organs of Samac, as well as other municipalities in Republika Srpska. What structure did this instruction have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instruction does not exempt anyone. It applied to all municipal secretariats for economy. They were bound to act pursuant to this instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the way you understand this instruction in view of what you were involved in at the time. And in practice, how did this function? How was this procedure that was envisaged at the level of Republika Srpska applied in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I briefly touched upon this issue yesterday. I said that the Crisis Staff had issued an order concerning the storage of spoils of war in the agricultural collective of Obudovac and the state-owned company Budva. It concerned the goods which had been requisitioned from the individuals by police organs. It applied to all non-certified goods which were then stored in one of these two facilities, in one of these two warehouses. Meanwhile, appropriate proceedings with the view of establishing the owners of this property were being followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, as a lawyer, the spoils of war, is this a legal category and when is this concept used and applied?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a normal category in times of war, and this particular concept exists legally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In Article 1 of this instruction, we have a government decision that is mentioned that was published a number -- in the issue of the Official Gazette number 8/92. What is this about?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A decree on the compulsory handover of spoils of war acquired by other means to the commodity reserves had been passed, and this instruction concerns practical arrangements, that is, how this decree should be implemented in practice and which particular organs were to be involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 3 and 4 of -- Articles 3 and 4 of this instruction, how did this function in the territory of the Samac municipality? Just a brief explanation, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the relevant authority, be it a civilian court or a military court, passes a decision and hands over the relevant goods, the relevant commodities to the municipality, the competent court registers this type of property, this type of commodities, and then a board -- a commission is established, which then hands over these goods to the republican commodity reserves. Members of this commission come from the Secretariat for Agriculture, from the Ministry of the Police and the Defence, and also the Ministry for Agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. As an employee of municipal organs, do you know if your colleagues, your co-workers, respected the provisions of this instruction? I am referring to the members of the relevant secretariat as well.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the Secretariat for Economy established at one point in time a commission which worked pursuant to the instruction for the implementation of the said decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D102/1 and D102/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document that I would like to discuss is R20. In fact, consisting of four documents. These are the pay lists of a pharmacy -- of municipal pharmacy for month of May 1992. That's the first document. The second is the pay list for the month of June 1992, also for the pharmacy of Bosanski Samac. The third is the pay list for July 1992, also for the pharmacy. And then there is a handwritten document for -- which is a list of employees present in the pharmacy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: You have given us a document RH27. Are you going to tender that document, or have you rejected it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: RH27 I will introduce, Your Honour. But now I'm -- maybe that's our mistake in your cover. We are now on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will introduce also. Maybe that's just the order how we put it. But we will come to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Lukic -- not to dwell too long on this matter. These are payrolls of the pharmacy for the months of May, June, July 1992. And as far as I can see, the document concerns attendance as the basis for salaries. Tell us briefly, in this particular case what is the ethnic background of the person who is the manager of the Bosanski Samac pharmacy, on the basis of the information that we have for these several months.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pharmacy in question is a state-owned pharmacy. The owner is Almasa Juskovic. She's a Muslim lady, and she's still the manager of this pharmacy even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did she return at one point in time after the war in Samac and is now back to her previous position, or did she keep it throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She stayed in Samac throughout that period of time and she kept her position there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please, for this document, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question. I've been reminded by my colleagues. Still on this list, please. What is the ethnic background of other employees of this pharmacy?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almasa is a Muslim. Zorka is -- this woman has a Muslim surname and a Serb name. Ruza is a Serb woman and Jovanka Petrovic and also a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Excuse me for the inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The payroll you introduced, May, June, July, and the list of employees in the Bosanski Samac pharmacy will be Exhibits D103A/1 and ter, D103B/1 and ter, D103C/1 and ter, and D103D/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter may have missed one name on the list of employees. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, when you asked the witness to describe the ethnicity on the list of employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters say that they didn't catch all the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Your Honour, I will try to clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Zorka Hadzialijagic, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim surname, but she's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe she's married to a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Rasida Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Muslim lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ruza Popovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Jovanka Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb lady too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Almasa Jusufovic, who was the manager of the pharmacy, what is her ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, it's about time for a break now. Shall we take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break for 20 minutes. We'll resume at 18.05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Now we are going to discuss a document R21/1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Number 1 is the pay list for the month of May 1992 for the company of waterworks Samac. It's a list consisting of 11 persons. The second pay list is for the month of June 1992 for the same company, a list consisting of 10 persons. The third document is also a pay list for the month of July 1992, same company, consisting of six persons. Then the fourth document is a list of workers -- employees for a kind of specification for the month of June 1992, consisting of 10 persons. And the last one is a document with a handwritten date on the top right-hand corner. The date is 16th of June, 1992. It's a request by the waterworks company to the executive board -- the municipal executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, this first document that we're looking for is for May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So far you have explained the mechanism of how the salaries were paid out. Can we agree that the list of employees is -- that the employees on the list are of mixed ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are different -- from different ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's all right. We don't have to go into details. We have the list here for July and June. Then we have a list for June 1992. And now, this last document, the request, I would just like to comment on it on a couple of points. Do you have it in front of you? Could you please put it on the ELMO so that the clients can see it. Okay. Very well. In June 1992, according to your personal knowledge, what were the technical problems, if there were any, regarding the Samac waterworks? Very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was on the first or the second day that I explained that one of the problems, which was a consequence of the war, was the lack of electricity. Since we have installations here that use pumps, which require electricity in order to operate, then there were bottlenecks and stoppages in this case, also due to intense shelling, the waterworks installations were destroyed, especially the pumping stations and the water collection network. This is why we needed expert labour or experts, technicians, who would be able to work on the maintenance of the waterworks and the sewage system, because that is one of the vital facilities during wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information about the fact that there was an attempt in 1992 to bomb the waterworks facilities in Samac from the air?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the early evening hours a helicopter flew over -- or it was a small airplane, actually, from the direction of Croatia and Slavonski Samac, which dropped several shells in the area of the waterworks facility, also the post office, and the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was this? Can you establish the date when this happened?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was in the autumn of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to this request, whereby the public enterprise of Vodovod, the waterworks in Samac, is seeking the opinion of the executive council regarding the work obligation. I'm interested in the following: The first two persons on the list are, as far as I can see, and in accordance with the earlier list, were key officials. They were the coordinators. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What does this term mean, this wording, whereby they say "On behalf of the company state that they are requesting work without set work hours"? Could you please explain to us what does that mean practically.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that the state of the installations was such that it was very alarming and that it was quite possible for the equipment to be disrupted and for blockages to occur in the sewage system, which would then bring about an epidemic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did these two management officials request for unlimited work hours, around-the-clock work in order to prevent such a thing from happening?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely why they requested it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's move to the second group of employees. We've dealt with this first group. When you look at these names -- and perhaps you know them personally. When you look at their names and last names, can you tell us of what ethnicity are these people listed from 3 to 6.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This group was meant to work as follows: 12 through 12. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that these name, these people would work for 12 hours and rest for 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that means that they would not be working all day.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There would be two persons per shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And when you look at this list, do you perhaps remember whether these people worked in the waterworks before the conflict broke out on the 17th of April, 1992, who remained in their jobs? Can you please tell us what you know about this.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a number of them, and they were employees of the waterworks. I don't know the last two persons under 10 and 11. I don't know whether they were employed at the waterworks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: In the order that the documents were introduced, they will be -- for the list of May 1992, with 11 names, it will be Exhibit D104A/1 and ter. For the second document, payrolls for June 1992, it will be -- with 10 names, it will be D104B/1 and ter. For the third document of July 1992, six names, it will be Exhibit D104D/1 and ter. For the fourth document dated June 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I thought this last one for the July one should be C. 104C.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Yes, C. Just to make things clear for the list of July 1992, with six names, it will be D104C/1 and ter. The fourth document, of June 1992 with 10 names, it will be Exhibit D104D/1 and ter. And the final and fifth document, the request dated 16th of June, 1992, it will be Exhibit D104E/1 and ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Registrar. The next document that I would like to discuss with the witness is internal number R22, consisting of three documents /1, 2, and 3. The first document is -- I don't know what is the order, but in my documents it's a pay list for the month of July 1992, company -- a social company Usce Bosne. I have actually the pay list from May until June, but I don't know how the order is in your documents, so maybe I can start from the month of May. Is it okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have May, June, and July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct. So I will start with May. Because my order is something different, but in order to have a logical order. So the first document is the pay list for month of May 1992. It's a state company Usce Bosne. It's a pay list consisting of -- just a moment. It' consisting of 45 employees, three-pages document. The second one is also a pay list for the month of June 1992, the same company, three pages. And the third is a pay list for the month of July, 1992, same company, consisting of 24 employees in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, could you please tell me what this company Usce Bosne is. What was its line of work?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company Usce Bosne deals with gravel and cement products, so it produces cement products, tiles, paving for blocks for streets, and all kinds of concrete goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was that the company that was meant to repair damaged facilities and work on reconstruction?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I assume the documents speak for themselves -- but I assume that here too the ethnic composition of the employees was also mixed in this company, according to these lists.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see here that there are members of all three ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And these are the payrolls in accordance with the principle that permission was asked from the executive council and that funds were transferred to bank accounts. It worked under that same principle.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me now so that we can clarify it -- this is the payroll for May. Under number 1, is Mr. Marko Arandzic, the managing officer. In the column where it says "salary," it states on the military list. What does that mean? Did that man work? And if he did, how was he paid? Did he have both military and civilian duties? Could you please explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see on this list that he did not receive a salary for his work under the work obligation, even though he did perform that duty and was a managing officer. But he did receive compensation through the brigade or through the military, and this salary was issued by the government or by the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There are a couple of other names like that but --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the principle is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We won't go into details about that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not receive salaries under two criteria: He did work in this company the entire time, but he did have an assignment -- a regular assignment in the military. He did and so did the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have a number, please, for these three documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The payroll for May 1992 will be Exhibit D105A/1 and ter. The payroll for June 1992 will be Exhibit D105B/1 and ter. The payroll for July 1992 will be Exhibit D105C/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document I would like to discuss is R23, consisting of -- it's a four-pages document. It's a kind of request from the hospital to the executive board. In total it's seven requests with regard to the fuel, month of August 1992. And the last one is July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me, Mr. Lukic, briefly what does this document deal with, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because I paid for this fuel. This is -- this has to do with the work of the hospital, or rather, the operation of the haemodialysis department that assisted patients with kidney conditions. It processed about 50 patients a day. The largest problem, in addition medicine and everything else that was needed for haemodialysis was the problem of insufficient electrical power supply, or rather, there was no electrical power supply at all. I told you that the power grid had been disrupted and disconnected from the power source, so we had to use generators in order to organise the system of dialysis because patients could not go without it for more than two days. So this is just one part of the request that we filed. We had a large generator which enabled 50 patients to be hooked to the system simultaneously. So this is just one part of our request for fuel to be allotted to us in order to power the generator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During the following year, 1993, was dialysis -- the haemodialysis kept on functioning despite the war operations in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The dialysis worked non-stop throughout the war. It still operates today. Today they serve 75 patients a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Although this is not your field, but do you happen to know whether haemodialysis was provided to all residents of Samac irrespective of their ethnicity during war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was provided to all patients, regardless of their ethnicity. Because these people underwent dialysis before the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The manager of this medical department --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The last answer is purely speculation. It doesn't add anything to the proceedings. He hasn't provided any information on who these patients were, how he knows that they were there before, after, the names of them. It's just pure speculation. It has no probative value at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. It could be that he meant that the dialysis facilities were operating even before the war. It's certainly true that he hasn't identified anybody, so he can't be certain that it was the same patients. That's accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just one more question: Chief of this medical department is Dr. Sisic. Did you know Dr. Sisic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was the coordinator at the hospital Dr. Nogic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Nogic was the coordinator of the medical centre. Now we're dealing with the secondary medical services, and Dr. Nogic was the coordinator of the primary medical services.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. I thought it was all the same, but apparently it's not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D106/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise. D106/1, and ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. The next one is R26. This is a -- sorry. This next document is R26. This is a letter from Posavina Brigade - it's a military unit - to executive board. The number is 1243/92, dated 11th of August, 1992, signed by the commander, Mr. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, we will turn to another area now. Please tell me now, this document was addressed to the executive council, wasn't it? Can you comment on the objective of this memo.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was of an informative nature. It was sent to the executive council, and it specified which actions were taken by the brigade with respect to military conscripts and with respect to the transportation of goods. I think that here this text pertains to military conscripts. I think it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned this earlier, but I would like now to focus on item 1. Can you tell us, please, people who were military conscripts, aged between 18 and 60, who issued these passes for them in order to be able to leave the zones?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The passes were issued by military units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Item 2, can you please comment on this. "To prevent uncontrolled transport of goods outside -- export of goods outside of the territory of the zone of responsibility of this brigade." This is mentioned in the preamble, in fact. Can you please tell us what this means.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the president of the executive council, when he explained this decision to us, told us that the military unit had learned that a lot of military conscripts were exporting their personal property to Serbia, because they had their families there. And then they were using the time -- their time in order to transport these goods. So by way of this order, they wanted to prevent these goods from being exported, or rather, they wanted to give prior consent to the military conscript in order to enable them to export some goods in a controlled manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So this topic had nothing to do with civilian organs. It was strictly within the domain of the military authorities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a purely military matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number for this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D107/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is R27. This is a two-page document with the title, "Instructions on the implementation of the decree on allowing the temporary use of abandoned farmland, farm buildings, farm machinery and implements", issued by the Minister of Agriculture of Republika Srpska on the 22nd of August, 1992, signed by the minister or someone on behalf of the minister - I'm not so sure - at that time. Yes. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me, Mr. Lukic, whether you were familiar with this instruction and with the decree that preceded it. What was the objective of this and what did it look like in practice?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Minister for Agriculture, Waterworks, and Forestry passed this instruction on allowing the temporary use of abandoned farmland, farm buildings, farm machinery and implements. And I spoke about that when I said that the Secretariat for Agriculture had adopted decisions on using funds for autumn planting. That decision was passed pursuant to this instruction, and it pertained to abandoned property that was temporarily given to certain individuals for temporary use, without touching into the ownership structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Item 3 of this instruction specifies that this decision is passed by the relevant municipal organ. Can you tell us what administrative organ was relevant to pass this in Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Secretariat for Economy, office for agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Item 4 mentions some kind of a commission that had to draw up a record. Please tell me what commission it was, and can you explain to us what constituted abandoned land. Why was it necessary to use this land and to work this land?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat for Economy in cooperation with the municipal land surveying agency created a commission which in the field had to identify a plot of land in accordance with land surveying plans, meaning a plot of land that had been registered appropriately in the land records and which had an owner. Then the commission issued a decision specifying that the land was owned by such and such person but was temporarily awarded to somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Why was it important to work the land regularly? Why wasn't it just left to decay?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a law in our territory which was in force in 1992 and throughout that all land had to be worked for the simple reason that we couldn't allow it to overgrow and turn into wilderness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would that reduce the quality of the arable land?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The quality would remain the same; however, later on one would have to invest a lot of effort to cultivate the land again and use it appropriately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since you said that temporary use did not mean that the land was confiscated from its previous owners, can you please tell us whether this abandoned land was owned by all three ethnic groups in Samac municipality or this applied only to certain ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied to all three ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's give an example. If a Serb left his land, what happened with that land? Was this decree applied to that land as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same instruction applied to everyone regardless of whether they were Serbs, Croats, or Muslims, because there was a law on compulsory cultivation of land. Therefore, if the rightful owner was not cultivating his or her land, then somebody else could be given temporary custody of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Would you be able to give us some idea as to the amount of farm property we're talking about? And also, apart from saying "all three ethnic groups", would you be able to go beyond that a little bit and maybe give us some idea again as to the breakdown of the property? That might be useful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are speaking about what land was mostly regulated by this decree, I have to say that the largest part of the land was owned by Croats, and then by Serbs and Muslims. And as to the area of the land, that would be some 6 to 700 hectares of arable land.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Can we have a number for this exhibit, this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D108/1 and D108/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document that I would like to discuss is R31. This is a two-page document. It's a letter. It's information sent by Red Cross -- local organisation of Red Cross of Samac to the executive board. It's kind of information on the activities of president of the Samac Municipal Red Cross and the head of Samac hospital in collecting expendable supplies for the haemodialysis centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was sent to the executive council in February 1993. I don't know if you remember what the document was all about. If you do, please give us your opinion about this document.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it. The executive council had sent these two individuals, the coordinator of the hospital, Mr. Sisic, and the president of the Red Cross, Mr. Velimir Maslic, to visit a number of places in Belgrade in order to secure adequate assistance for the haemodialysis department of this hospital because the situation at that time was already critical; that is to say, we were no longer enable to ensure resources for the purchase of otherwise very expensive equipment which was used on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you comment on the last paragraph of this memo. What interests me in particular is the relation with the Belgrade office of the WHO, whose representatives had visited them in the meantime. Do you know if there had been any contacts with the officials of the WHO for the purposes of resolving this situation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was involved in some intensive talks with the Medecins sans Frontier. And throughout that period of time and even later in 1996, 1997, and 1998 they were helping us in the purchase of this equipment, namely, these dialysis. They even visited the haemodialysis department on one occasion and came to the municipality on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During the war as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the war as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number for this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D109/1 and D109/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is IO1. It's a two-page document regarding official travels, dated 9th of June, 1992, issued by executive board -- municipal executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you briefly tell us something about this particular decision. It was an operational document. Just a brief explanation, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This instruction was signed by the president of the executive council. It concerns official travels of the coordinators of economic and other departments. This is an official travel authorisation -- I mean, the official travel authorisations could be issued only by the executive council so that they had information on the whereabouts of the coordinator, where he went, how long he stayed, and what the purpose of the travel was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you say "the coordinator," you're probably referring to the manager of the relevant company.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the relevant company or the relevant institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the other page I can see a list of the persons to whom these expenses were to be paid from the budget. What about other companies? Who covered their travel expenses?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the executive council that authorised such travels, but they had to secure resources for their travels.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you're referring to the companies who sent their employees to such travels, and you want to say that they had to cover for their expenses.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Among those employees who went on official travels for various reasons, either from these companies or some other institutions or organs, who were they? Who was covered by this authorisation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for instance, you have here Mr. Nogic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D110/1 and D110/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is IO2, a one-page document. It's two pages of translation. It's a document regarding the formation of commission for the assignment of houses for the temporary use pursuant to a decision of the executive committee, issued -- dated 19th of July, 1992, issued by executive board -- or municipal executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Mr. Lukic. Here we see that a commission was established, but this is preceded by a decision on the assignment of some property. Are we talking about the composition of this commission in this document? What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This commission did not issue decisions on the temporary use of abandoned property. Its task concerned the individuals who had already been issued such decisions on authorisation -- approvals on temporary use. They had to make appropriate record on what was found on arrival in such house or on that property and to attach this record to the relevant decision on the temporary use of abandoned property. I believe that I addressed the issue yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It was a decree issued at the level of the republic that governed these issues.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D111/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the next document which I would like to discuss is IO3. It's a request for issuance of decision for the work assignment, dated 7th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This memo was sent by the executive council to the municipal department for National Defence in Samac. In light of what you have already told us, is it true that regardless of who requested the work assignment, the whole procedure had to go through the ministry at the level of the republic? They could not adopt the appropriate decision on their own. What is the relationship between the relevant organ at the municipal level and the ministry at the level of the republic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the executive council issues a request for work assignment to the Secretariat for National Defence, which is an autonomous organ under the jurisdiction of the Ministry for Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D112/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is IO4, dated the 11th of September, 1992, signed by -- issued by the executive board. It's an order to prohibit payment for cattle and other agriculture products purchased.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, I don't personally fully understand this particular decision. Can you explain it to us, please, if you know. I see that the addressees are agricultural collectives, the Pik company, a socially-owned company, and I see that there is a provision here of the SAO Semberija and Majevica. Just briefly, what was the purpose of this decision? What was its objective?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you about the decision of the Crisis Staff, that is, an order of the Crisis Staff concerning the spoils of war and the instruction and the decree issued to that effect by Republika Srpska concerning collection and handover of spoils of war. This order pertains to this issue. Now, what was this all about? It had come to our notice that individuals had found abandoned cattle, wandering cattle in the fields, and they then addressed themselves -- they would come to these various organs and try to sell this cattle. They were not dealing with anybody else's property but only with the property in respect of which there was adequate ownership records. And when we noticed that these individuals were selling two, three, or more cows to these companies, we issued an order to these companies whereby we banned any payment to be made on account of this cattle sale. Eventually this cattle was made part of the republic commodity reserves in accordance with the appropriate decree, and it was not paid for to those individuals who had handed it over to the relevant organs without adequate papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but the purpose was to prevent these individual attempts of fraud.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever wanted to obtain any gain illegally had to be sanctioned. So whenever we knew of such cases, we issued relevant decisions or instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D113/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I believe it's practically 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it's 7.00. And according to the agreed hours for this witness, you have one hour more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have virtually six or seven documents to discuss and maybe a couple of questions in addition, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think I am well below --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. You have one hour more. So we'll adjourn and continue tomorrow at 14.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
